title: fix: Safe Apps permissions modal alignment
description: ## What it solves Resolves: [WA-3447](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-3447/safe-apps-permissions-modal-shield-icon-left-aligned-and-content-top) On the Safe Apps permissions step of the info modal ("Manage the features Safe Apps can use"), the shield icon sat hard against the left edge of the modal body while the title beside it stayed centered. ## How this PR fixes it Fix is `mx-auto` on the icon. Measured in Storybook: | | icon `x` | icon centre | modal centre | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | before | 250 | 262 | 450 | | ticket's proposed fix | 250 | 262 | 450 | | this PR | 438 | **450** | **450** | Also in this PR, beyond the icon: - **`mb-2` on the icon** and **`mx-[75px]` removed from the title** — AC item 4. The 75px inline margin was a faithful port of production's `margin: '0 75px'`, but in a 450px modal it forced the title to wrap with "use" orphaned on line 2. Pre-existing on production, not a regression; removed here since the modal was already open. - **List container `mt-2 ml-4` → `m-4 ... gap-4`** — even spacing between the permission rows instead of relying on the checkbox's own margins. - **`cursor-pointer` on the permission row** (`PermissionCheckbox`) — the row was fully clickable but showed a text cursor. findings.claim: loaders: [mswLoader] is declared on both the story meta and on the Default story, registering it twice, whereas sibling stories declare it only on the meta.

FEATURES lacks an `as const` assertion, so AllowedFeatures resolves to plain string and every `as AllowedFeatures[]` cast becomes a no-op, meaning a misspelled feature name would still type-check; this includes new casts added in SafeAppsInfoModal/index.stories.tsx.
loaders: [mswLoader] is declared a second time even though meta already sets it, which does not match the documented pattern of using an empty Default story object.
The same ineffective `as AllowedFeatures[]` cast appears again here, repeating the misleading type assertion.

The `as AllowedFeatures[]` cast has no effect because FEATURES in types.ts is not declared with `as const`, making AllowedFeatures resolve to plain string; the cast therefore validates nothing and misleadingly implies the values are checked.

The story calls local.setItem with a hardcoded storage key at the top level of the file, so it writes to real localStorage as soon as the file loads. This overwrites the viewer's actual Storybook localStorage, the change persists across other stories and reloads, and the key duplicates the unexported BROWSER_PERMISSIONS constant from useBrowserPermissions.ts, so renaming that constant would silently break the story.
The same ineffective `as AllowedFeatures[]` cast appears again here, repeating the misleading type assertion.
Part of the scroll layout's Tailwind classes (min-h-0 flex-auto) live here, separate from the corresponding CSS module rules, spreading a single layout fix across multiple files.

The new postcss-based style test only verifies the CSS module half of the scroll fix; reverting the Tailwind classes in index.tsx (lines 121/137) or Slider.tsx (line 71) would break the long-list-scrolls behavior without causing this or any other test to fail.
The file contains a sixth local copy of the postcss findRule/declOf helper functions, duplicating the same pair already present in five other styles.test.ts files across the codebase.

The .sliderContainer rules (flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto) here hold only half of the scroll layout fix, with the other half implemented as Tailwind classes in index.tsx and Slider.tsx.

The scroll layout fix is split between Tailwind utility classes here and CSS module rules elsewhere, so the fix only works if every nesting level is set up correctly in both places; the long inline class string at this line also keeps growing, which is the pattern the relevant convention warns against.
BROWSER_PERMISSIONS is not exported from this file even though its value is duplicated as a hardcoded string in the story, creating a hidden coupling between the two files.

local.setItem('SafeApps__browserPermissions', …) runs at module import time and writes to real localStorage with no cleanup, and preview.tsx never clears it, so this data can leak into another story (SafeApps.stories.tsx) that renders the same component, making its rendered output depend on story load order.
The storage key is hard-coded instead of importing BROWSER_PERMISSIONS from useBrowserPermissions.ts, which is currently private, so if the key is ever renamed the story will silently seed nothing.

The slider container's overflow was changed from hidden to overflow-y: auto, but nextSlide and prevSlide never reset scrollTop and no key forces a remount, so the next slide keeps the previous slide's scroll position. Since all slides are stretched to the tallest slide's height, this can make a subsequent slide such as the safety warning appear blank until the user scrolls back up.
A shrink-0 Tailwind class here is another piece of the scroll layout fix that lives outside the CSS module, contributing to the same split-layout problem.
